DECISION: Abacus is a greenfield project with no users. Always choose the best design over backward compatibility. No need for deprecated params, shims, or migration paths — just make the best API. This applies to Go function signatures, CLI flags, scanner protocols, and schema evolution.

FACT: Abacus edge ingestion uses INSERT OR REPLACE (upsert) so re-scanning is idempotent. Both BulkUpsertNodes and InsertEdge now upsert. CLI query default limit is 1000 (was 50). React Router scanner auto-detects route files via (1) hardcoded common locations including App.tsx/MainApp.tsx, (2) glob fallback searching tsx/jsx files for <Route content. All scanners have within-file dedup via Set+counter (#N suffix).

FACT: Abacus project uses go.mod module path github.com/mjn/abacus. Cobra CLI with Version injected via ldflags. Config loaded from .abacus/config.yaml with YAML v3. Makefile targets: build, install, test, lint, clean.

FACT: Abacus scan pipeline after March 2026 fixes — schema v2 (no UNIQUE edge constraint), route IDs include file-derived prefix (route:METHOD-routerName:path), edge IDs include field name (field_relation:fieldName), within-file dedup via Set+counter (#N suffix), test files excluded by hardcoded filter, ignorePaths config for directory exclusion. Default ignorePaths: node_modules, dist, build, .git. Live progress output to stderr during scan.

FACT: Abacus SQLite schema uses modernc.org/sqlite v1.46.1 (pure Go). Tables: nodes (5 kinds, JSON properties, FTS5 triggers), edges (adjacency list, UNIQUE(src,dst,kind), CASCADE delete), schema_version. Pragmas: WAL, NORMAL sync, FK ON, 64MB cache, 5s busy timeout.

FACT: In Claude Code sandbox, Go module cache at ~/go/pkg is read-only. Set GOMODCACHE to a project-local .gomodcache/ dir (already in .gitignore) with GONOSUMDB=* GONOSUMCHECK=*. Do NOT rely on /tmp/.claude_scratch existing — it's not available in CI.

FACT: Integration test repos for abacus are in ./test_repos/ relative to the abacus project root (/Users/mjn/workplace/abacus/test_repos/). Do NOT look in ~/workplace/pcom_workplace/hourly or other locations.

FACT: When abacus is installed via go install to ~/go/bin/, the scanners/ directory is NOT next to the binary. Users must set ABACUS_SCANNERS_PATH=/path/to/abacus/scanners for auto-detection to generate correct scanner commands. Future fix: publish scanners as npm packages so config uses npx @abacus/scanner-express (tracked in bead aba-5nz).

LEARNED: abacus init detectProject must scan subdirectory package.json files for monorepo support. Root package.json may only have client-side deps (@orpc/client) while server deps (express, @orpc/server) live in backend/package.json. Similarly, Prisma schema may be at backend/prisma/schema.prisma not root. Fix: iterate os.ReadDir entries and merge deps from all immediate subdirectory package.json files. Also detect any @orpc/* prefix, not just @orpc/server.

LEARNED: abacus init --force flag re-detects scanners and overwrites config.yaml. Without --force, init exits early if .abacus/config.yaml exists. Auto-detection checks package.json deps for express, react-router/react-router-dom, @orpc/server, and filesystem for prisma/schema.prisma. Scanner paths resolved via ABACUS_SCANNERS_PATH env var or binary-relative probing.

LEARNED: Abacus scanners crash with 'not iterable' when config options are empty. Each scanner needs defaults: Express routeGlobs=['**/*.ts','**/*.js'], oRPC contractGlobs=['**/*.ts'], React Router auto-detects from common locations, Prisma falls back through subdirectory paths. Always use options?.field ?? default pattern.

LEARNED: Go exec.Command does NOT expand environment variables in command strings. Dollar-brace syntax like ${VAR}/path in config files will be passed literally. Use either absolute paths set during initialization or relative paths resolved at runtime. For path resolution, establish a canonical rule: relative paths are relative to the config file directory, not CWD.

LEARNED: Plan review with 4 specialized agents (architecture, simplicity, security, performance) caught 12 actionable issues including 2 critical ones: (1) InitSchema destructive migration silently destroys manual/agent-created nodes on schema version bump, (2) GetConnected bidirectional BFS becomes unusable when intermediate nodes are added without edge-kind filtering. Both were invisible during brainstorm/planning.

LEARNED: Scanner node/edge IDs must include source file context for global uniqueness. Express/oRPC route IDs changed from route:${METHOD}-${path} to route:${METHOD}-${routerName}:${path} where routerName is derived by stripping common prefixes (src/, backend/, routes/) and extensions (.routes.ts, .ts). Prisma edge IDs changed to include field name: edge:entity:${model}-field_relation:${fieldName}-entity:${target}. Without file context, routes like GET / from different router files collide.

PATTERN: Abacus DoS prevention layering — user-facing caps (maxAllowedDepth=10, maxAllowedLimit=500) live as consts in mcp/server.go handlers. Defense-in-depth caps (maxGetConnectedDepth=50) live in the repository function itself. Handler caps are tight for safety; repository caps are generous so internal callers (CLI, tests) retain full control. Same clamp-not-error pattern: silently reduce, never reject.

PATTERN: Abacus graph kind vocabulary has a single source of truth: db.AllNodeKinds and db.AllEdgeKinds slices in types.go. validate.go derives maps at init. stats.go and mcp iterate the slices. Adding a new kind requires: (1) add constant + append to All*Kinds in types.go, (2) update CHECK constraint + bump version in schema.go. Only 2 sync points now, down from 3.

PATTERN: Abacus two-pass scan pipeline — CLI scan.go orchestrates: (1) filter cfg.Scanners map by Phase field into scanPhaseConfigs/linkPhaseConfigs slices, (2) run scan-phase with 60s Runner, (3) ingest nodes+edges, (4) collect ScanNodeRef from route+entity nodes (or query DB if standalone linker run), (5) build knownNodeIDs map, (6) run link-phase with 5min Runner passing ExistingNodes+knownNodeIDs, (7) DeleteEdgesBySourceScanner then BulkUpsertEdges per linker. Runner.RunScanner accepts knownNodeIDs map[string]bool as 4th param for cross-scanner edge validation.

PATTERN: Claude Code plugin owner vs author distinction — marketplace.json uses 'owner' (marketplace-level), plugin.json uses 'author' (plugin-level). Same structure {name: string} but different key names. Version/category/keywords only exist in marketplace.json, not plugin.json.

PATTERN: Claude Code plugin requires TWO JSON files in .claude-plugin/: (1) plugin.json (minimal: name, description, author) and (2) marketplace.json (has $schema, owner, plugins[] array with version/category/keywords/source). For a single-plugin repo, source is './'. Commands go in commands/ as markdown with YAML frontmatter (description, argument-hint). Filenames become command names (/abacus-scan from abacus-scan.md). Command body is agent instructions, not user docs.

PATTERN: Exemplar-based pattern discovery — when users need to build something new, find an existing fully-wired example from their codebase. Traverse the graph for an entity with rich delegation chains, present the chain as an ordered file list (route→service→repository→entity). The system teaches users their own project conventions rather than generating boilerplate.

PATTERN: GetConnected needs edge-kind filtering for any graph that has multiple edge kinds at different abstraction levels. Without it, a 'show me the neighborhood' query returns everything — delegation chains, field relations, action references — creating noise. The filter is AND e.kind IN (...) in the recursive CTE clauses. This should have been built from the start but becomes critical when adding new edge kinds.

PATTERN: TS linker scanner (scanners/linker-ts/) architecture — 4-module pipeline: index.ts (stdin/stdout protocol, builds routeNodes/entityByName maps from ExistingNodes) → parser.ts (ts-morph Project setup, route iteration, shared depth-aware cache) → tracer.ts (depth-limited DFS through imports, visited-set cycle protection per trace, depth-aware transitive file entity cache shared across traces: Map<filePath, {entities: Set<string>, remainingDepth: number}>) → matcher.ts (PrismaClient variable resolution + prisma.model.method() AST chain walking). Linker emits only edges (nodes: never[]), edge kind: touches_entity. Cache correctness requires: (1) traceFile returns Set<string> transitive closure, (2) cache guarded by remainingDepth <= cached.remainingDepth, (3) overwrites on deeper re-exploration.

PATTERN: When a SQL recursive CTE result is needed for two queries (e.g. fetch nodes then fetch edges between those nodes), run the CTE once, collect IDs in the application layer, then use WHERE col IN (...) for the second query. In GetConnected this halved query cost. The args array is 2×len(nodes) because the same IDs appear in both IN clauses (src_id IN ... AND dst_id IN ...). Tradeoff: query string grows with node count, but graph traversals are depth-capped so the set is bounded.

PATTERN: When adding intermediate nodes to a graph (e.g., modules between routes and entities), ALWAYS keep the direct summary edge (touches_entity) alongside the detailed chain (delegates_to). Without the summary edge, all existing queries break because they need higher depth to reach the same nodes. Summary edges are like materialized views in a database — the detailed edges add resolution, the summary preserves compatibility.

PATTERN: When building agent skills that compose MCP tools, keep text reasoning (entity extraction, parsing, pattern generalization) in the skill prompt. Tools handle external state access (DB, filesystem, graph). This minimizes tool surface and leverages LLM strengths. Decision boundary: needs state access = tool, pure text reasoning = agent.

PATTERN: When the graph serves as an INDEX (not a classifier), avoid storing derived metadata like 'role' on nodes. The consuming agent reads the actual source file — classification is the agent's job at query time, not the scanner's job at scan time. This eliminated an entire config layer and all pattern-matching complexity from the module nodes plan.

PRINCIPLE: Abacus design goals are efficiency, accuracy, and queryability — NOT intelligence. Smart behavior comes from skills that compose Abacus with other tools. Abacus should be fast to scan, correct in its graph representation, and easy to query from any context (MCP, CLI, skills). When in doubt about adding a feature to Abacus core vs a skill: if it requires reasoning, it's a skill. If it requires data, it's Abacus.

PRINCIPLE: Abacus is a GRAPH + COVERAGE tool, not an agent. It captures: (1) structure of a system (routes, entities, modules, pages, delegation chains), (2) BDD coverage (step-to-action mapping, coverage reports), (3) action definitions (what steps map to what infrastructure). Everything beyond that — entity extraction from step text, Gherkin parsing, pattern recognition, code generation, decision-making — belongs to the consuming agent. Abacus becomes powerful THROUGH agents, not BY BEING one. This is the fundamental boundary: Abacus stores and queries the map, agents navigate it.
